title: How to Maintain Your HVAC System
h1: How Do You Maintain an HVAC System Year-Round?
description: Regular HVAC maintenance keeps your system running efficiently and helps prevent breakdowns. Here is what homeowners can do and what a technician checks.
quick_answer: Change the filter every one to three months, keep the outdoor unit clear, keep vents open, and check the condensate drain. Then have a professional tune-up once a year, ideally twice if you use both heating and cooling, to clean coils, test electrical parts and safety controls, and catch small problems early.
body:
An HVAC system doesn't need much from you, but it does need some attention. A little routine maintenance keeps it running efficiently, keeps your air cleaner, and helps you avoid the kind of breakdown that always seems to happen on the hottest day of the year.

What HVAC maintenance can you do yourself?

These tasks take minutes and make the biggest difference:

  1. Change the air filter. Check it monthly and replace it every one to three months, sooner with pets, allergies or wildfire smoke. A clogged filter is one of the most common reasons systems run poorly.
  2. Keep the outdoor unit clear. Trim plants back a couple of feet, rinse off leaves and dirt with a gentle hose spray, and keep trash cans and storage away from it.
  3. Keep supply vents and returns open. Closing vents in unused rooms doesn't save energy and can cause pressure problems.
  4. Check the condensate drain. Look for standing water in the pan near the indoor unit, and make sure water drips from the drain line outside when the AC runs.
  5. Test your thermostat at the start of each season. Replace batteries if it uses them.
  6. Test your CO alarms if you have a gas furnace.
  7. Listen and look. New noises, odd smells or short cycling are worth a call before they turn into a breakdown.

Leave anything involving electrical panels, gas lines or refrigerant to a professional.

What does a professional HVAC tune-up include?

A good tune-up goes well beyond a quick look. On the cooling side, a technician typically:

  • Cleans or checks the evaporator and condenser coils
  • Checks refrigerant pressures and looks for signs of a leak
  • Tests capacitors, contactors and electrical connections
  • Flushes the condensate drain
  • Measures airflow and temperature difference

On the heating side, a technician typically:

  • Inspects burners, the flame sensor and igniter
  • Checks the heat exchanger for cracks
  • Tests safety controls and venting
  • Checks gas pressure and combustion

How often should an HVAC system be serviced?

Once a year at minimum. If you use both heating and cooling, a visit in spring for the AC and in fall for the furnace or heat pump is ideal. In San Diego and Orange County, many homes lean on the AC for months at a time inland and use the heat on cold winter nights, so both sides get real use.

Heat pumps do both jobs with one system, so they work year-round and benefit from twice-a-year checkups.

What local conditions affect HVAC maintenance?

  • Salt air near the coast corrodes outdoor coils and fins faster. Rinsing the outdoor unit and regular coil checks help.
  • Santa Ana winds blow dust and debris into outdoor units.
  • Wildfire smoke loads up filters quickly.
  • Attic installations get very hot in summer, which is hard on equipment and makes leaks in attic ducts more costly.

Why does HVAC maintenance matter?

A clean, well-adjusted system cools and heats more evenly and doesn't have to work as hard. Maintenance also catches worn parts, like a weak capacitor or a dirty flame sensor, before they cause a no-cool or no-heat call. And it keeps safety controls on gas equipment working the way they should.

Many equipment manufacturers also expect regular professional maintenance, so keep your service records.

Signs your system needs service now

  • Warm air from the vents when the AC is on, or cool air when the heat is on
  • The system turning on and off every few minutes
  • Ice on the refrigerant lines or outdoor unit
  • Water around the indoor unit
  • Grinding, squealing or banging noises
  • A burning smell that lasts more than the first few minutes of the season

Don't wait for the next scheduled tune-up if you notice any of these. Turn the system off and have it checked.
faqs: How often should I change my HVAC filter?
Every one to three months for most homes. Check it monthly and replace it sooner if it looks gray, if you have pets or allergies, or during wildfire smoke.
Is annual HVAC maintenance really necessary?
Yes. A yearly tune-up keeps the system efficient, catches worn parts early and checks safety controls on gas equipment. Systems that run a lot benefit from twice-a-year visits.
When is the best time to schedule HVAC maintenance?
Spring for air conditioning and fall for heating. Booking before the busy season usually means more scheduling options.
Can I hose off my outdoor AC unit?
Yes, gently. Turn the power off, then rinse the fins from the inside out with a garden hose on low pressure. Avoid pressure washers, which bend the fins.
